title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 77-78
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 77 to 78 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'विश्वमूर्तिर्महामूर्तिर्दीप्तमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान्'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 77 to 78 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 77 to 78.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 77 to 78** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**विश्वमूर्तिर्महामूर्तिर्दीप्तमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान् । अनेकमूर्तिरव्यक्तः शतमूर्तिः शताननः ॥** **एको नैकः सवः कः किं यत्तत्पदमनुत्तमम् । लोकबन्धुर्लोकनाथो माधवो भक्तवत्सलः ॥**

The universe is his form, vast and radiant. The formless too is that God of gods. Of many forms, unmanifest, of a hundred shapes and a hundred faces. He is one, and yet he is in many forms. The sacrifice, the Who, the What, that supreme state is that God of gods. Kin of the worlds, lord of the worlds, Madhava, tender to his devotees.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 77 to 78 mean?
faq.a: The universe is his form, vast and radiant. The formless too is that God of gods. Of many forms, unmanifest, of a hundred shapes and a hundred faces. He is one, and yet he is in many forms. The sacrifice, the Who, the What, that supreme state is that God of gods. Kin of the worlds, lord of the worlds, Madhava, tender to his devotees.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
